subject: Summit Retail — post-incident stability remediation logbook
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@summitretail.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Summit Retail — interim RCA, mitigation plan, and next steps

Samira / Daniel,

Thanks for the bridge this morning. Attached is our interim RCA and a proposed remediation plan for the latency and 502 surge you observed on Tuesday morning (09/28). This memo summarizes the root cause findings, immediate mitigations we executed, and the corrective actions we are committing to over the next two weeks.

High-level summary:
- Root cause: KV-cache fragmentation after a spike in short-lived sessions combined with a model variant fallback that recompiled a quantized kernel under load, increasing per-request latency and raising error rates.
- Immediate mitigations applied: pinned model variant to the stable 1.4 runtime on your Dedicated pool; increased KV cache capacity for the affected shard; temporary traffic shaping to limit burst concurrency.

Requested next steps from Summit: please confirm a 1-hour maintenance window on Monday (10/04) so we can deploy the full remediation (cache rebalancing + kernel pre-warm) and run a post-deploy validation.

Attachments: 20270930_summit_rca.pdf (interim RCA), kv_cache_screenshot.png (cache metrics snapshot)

We will follow up by tomorrow with an ownership matrix and a short status cadence. Apologies again for the customer impact — we know this disrupted peak checkout flows.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0137

Subject: RE: Summit Retail — interim RCA, mitigation plan, and next steps

Jasmine — thanks for the write-up. Operational checklist below (I ran this past infra and runtime):

- Pre-deploy validation (owner: Markus): create a synthetic workload that reproduces short session spikes; verify KV cache entry churn metrics and QPS 99p latency baseline.
- Kernel pre-warm (owner: Grace): warm the quantized kernel paths for the 1.4 runtime on Summit's dedicated nodes; confirm no on-the-fly compilation.
- Cache rebalance (owner: Ben): increase shard allocation by 25% for the affected cache slice and drain/repopulate with warming TTL.
- Rollout plan (owner: Jasmine): coordinated maintenance window with Summit + stepwise traffic ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with canary checks.

I suggest we also loop in Jonas for exec visibility and for the customer comms approval. I'll prepare the synthetic test harness and share results by EOD Friday.

-Markus
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

Subject: Summit Retail — confirmed maintenance 10/04 02:00 PT + remediation steps and comms draft

Samira / Daniel,

Thanks for confirming availability. Summit — we have scheduled the maintenance for Mon 04 Oct 02:00–03:30 PT. The deployment is designed to be non-disruptive; we will perform the cache rebalance and kernel pre-warm behind a canary and ramp traffic as described below. If we detect error-rate regression during the canary, we will automatically rollback and notify you.

Planned sequence (high level):
- 02:00–02:10: deploy pre-checks and start canary on 10% traffic
- 02:10–02:25: run synthetic spike test, validate KV churn metrics and 99p latency
- 02:25–02:50: perform cache rebalance and kernel pre-warm on canary hosts
- 02:50–03:20: ramp to 50% and then 100% if canary is stable
- 03:20–03:30: post-deploy monitoring + customer verification call (15 minutes)

Customer comms (for approval):
Subject: Planned maintenance — brief stability work (Oct 4)
Body: Hello Summit customers — we will perform a brief maintenance window to improve inference stability; we expect no downtime but short degradation during Canary. If you rely on strict SLAs, please reach out to your customer success manager.

We will attach the final RCA after the deployment completes and the post-validation run is green.

Thanks — we will join your internal verification call at 03:20 PT.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Summit Retail — post-maintenance notes, results, and open actions

Team — quick closure note following the 10/04 maintenance and the validation window:

Outcome:
- Canary and full ramp completed successfully; 99p latency returned to baseline and 502 error rate dropped from 0.9% -> 0.02% during peak testing.
- The root cause confirmed: concurrent short-lived session churn caused cache eviction storms which, combined with a fallback compilation event on a subset of nodes, amplified tail latency.

Completed actions:
- Cache shard allocation increased by 25% (rolled back if adverse effects observed) — DONE.
- Quantized kernel pre-warm implemented and verified — DONE.
- Traffic shaping during peak windows added to Summit tenant config — DONE.

Open / follow-up items (owners & due dates):
- Monitoring: add a dedicated alert that tracks KV churn rate and triggers an automated canary (owner: Grace, due: 2027-10-12).
- Capacity: review Dedicated pool sizing to avoid repeated rebalancing at peaks (owner: Jonas, due: 2027-10-15).
- Post-mortem doc: finalize and publish the full RCA to the shared Drive and send to Summit execs (owner: Jasmine, due: 2027-10-08) — note: draft in Drive now.

Customer note: Samira replied that overall checkout latency improved and they saw fewer failed checkouts in the subsequent 48h window. They requested we keep them updated on the monitoring alert tuning.

I'll put these actions into the exec readout and the renewal follow-up pack. Great cross-team response — thank you.

-Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
